paths.title: Your first paint
paths.blurb: From an empty window to your own paint on the car in iRacing: the two settings that matter, zones, render and reload.

quiz.q: iRacing reads two pictures for every car. Which two?
a: The paint and the spec map
The paint and a PSD file
The number and the sponsor sheet
quiz.why: The paint holds the colours; the spec map says how metallic, rough and glossy each pixel is. Shokker builds both.

quiz.q: What goes in the iRacing User ID box?
quiz.why: It is your Customer ID, not your car number. Every file is named with it.

quiz.q: If the ID or the car folder is wrong, what does iRacing do?
quiz.why: iRacing never reports it; it simply finds no file with your name and falls back.

quiz.q: Which file keeps the numbers, logos and body paint apart so zones can target the body only?
a: A layered PSD, XCF or ORA template
quiz.why: A layered template keeps them on separate layers; a flat file can only be separated by colour.

quiz.q: Which of the six words changes ONLY the shine?
quiz.why: A pattern is a visible design; a spec pattern changes only the shine.

quiz.q: You add a zone and press PICK COLOR FROM CAR. What does clicking a colour on the paint do?
a: The zone grabs every pixel of that colour
quiz.why: Each click adds another colour to the zone's catch; it chooses pixels, it does not recolour them.

quiz.q: Two zones want the same pixel. Which one gets it?
a: The zone higher in the list
The zone with the brighter colour
quiz.why: The first zone in the list has the highest priority; lower zones only get what is left.

quiz.q: What size does RENDER build?
a: The size of the template you opened (2048 or 1024)
quiz.why: Size is not a setting: Shokker renders at the size of the template you opened.

quiz.q: After a render, how do you see it in iRacing without restarting?
a: Press Ctrl+R in iRacing (Reload Car Textures)
quiz.why: Alt+Tab to iRacing and press Ctrl+R there; the car flashes white and shows the new files.

paths.title: Spec mastery
paths.blurb: The shine picture iRacing reads, channel by channel: metal, roughness, the backwards clearcoat, the lighting mask, the iron rules and the tools to read real values.

quiz.q: What does the spec map tell iRacing?
a: How metallic, rough and glossy each spot is
quiz.why: The colour file says what colour a spot is; the spec map says what it is made of.

quiz.q: R (metallic) at 255 means…
quiz.why: 0 is plain paint, plastic or glass; 255 is solid mirror metal.

quiz.q: A real chrome needs which paint colour under it?
a: Any colour, it does not matter
quiz.why: Metal shows the paint colour in its reflection, so chrome needs a very light paint.

quiz.q: G (roughness) 0 is…
quiz.why: 0 is a perfect mirror and 255 is dead flat.

quiz.q: Which clearcoat value is MAXIMUM gloss?
quiz.why: Blue runs backwards: 16 is the strongest, shiniest coat and bigger numbers get duller.

quiz.q: What do clearcoat values 0 to 15 mean?
quiz.why: 0 to 15 mean no clearcoat; a normal Shokker render raises blue to at least 16.

quiz.q: Alpha 0 in the spec map means…
a: iRacing lighting is switched off for that spot
quiz.why: Alpha is not transparency: 255 is normal lighting, 128 reduced, 0 lighting killed.

quiz.q: Roughness may go below 15 only when…
quiz.why: Rule two: roughness is at least 15 wherever metal is under 240; only mirror chrome may go lower.

quiz.q: High metal and LOW roughness reads as…
quiz.why: Low/low is wet paint, high metal + low roughness is chrome, low metal + high roughness is flat, high/high is chalky raw metal.

quiz.q: In a zone's stack, what comes LAST?
a: The spec overlays (surface detail, no colour)
quiz.why: Base first, then patterns, then up to five spec overlays that touch only the spec.

quiz.q: What does a Feel do?
a: Sets the three channel sliders at once
quiz.why: Feels are one-click spec tweaks; the disk icon saves your own.

quiz.q: Where do you read exact spec values from a spot on the car?
quiz.why: The Material Sampler shows each channel and the min, max and mean values of a sampled spot.

paths.title: Pro workflows
paths.blurb: Work the way the pros do: layered templates, zones locked to layers, vinyl-true decals, the right file names and Trading Paints.

quiz.q: Which template should you open?
a: The template for the same car you drive
quiz.why: Pick the template for the car you drive; the layer tree then shows its guide layers.

quiz.q: A zone locked to a layer owns pixels where…
a: That layer is solid and the art above it is not
quiz.why: It owns pixels where the layer is solid (alpha 128+) and the art above it is under 128.

quiz.q: You want a candy body without touching numbers and logos. Where does the change go?
a: On the whole car with no layer limit
On the body paint layer only
quiz.why: A zone limited to the body layer cannot touch the decals; a whole-car colour finish paints over them.

quiz.q: Which guide layers must be OFF before you render?
quiz.why: Wire and Mask are guides; if visible they end up in your paint. Car_Mandatory stays as the template has it.

quiz.q: Decal Rescue makes numbers and sponsors look like…
a: Real vinyl: flat, satin or gloss
quiz.why: You pick a vinyl type (Flat Vinyl, Satin Decal, Gloss Decal), each with its own metal, roughness and coat.

quiz.q: Custom Number writes car_num_<ID>.tga. When does iRacing load it?
a: Only when Graphics > Hide Car Numbers is ON
quiz.why: car_num_ is loaded with Hide Car Numbers ON; car_<ID>.tga (Sim-Stamped) is the default.

quiz.q: What is the spec file called?
quiz.why: Every render writes the paint plus car_spec_<ID>.tga, named with your Customer ID.

quiz.q: What does Trading Paints take for the shine?
a: A .mip file iRacing builds from car_spec_<ID>.tga
quiz.why: Trading Paints takes your spec only as the .mip iRacing builds; never upload the Shokker project.
